name: APT27
affiliation_detail:
In March 2025, the DOJ unsealed indictments identifying two APT27 members: Yin Kecheng (active since 2013, linked to the MSS) and Zhou Shuai/"Coldface" (a first-generation Chinese patriotic hacker from the 1990s who operated through his company Shanghai Heiying). According to the indictment, both operated as freelancers/contractors, conducting intrusions for the MSS and MPS while also hacking for personal profit and selling stolen data through i-Soon — the Chinese hacking-for-hire firm exposed by a February 2024 document leak.
Earlier attribution was based on circumstantial evidence: SecureWorks (2015) assessed with "moderate confidence" that TG-3390 has a Chinese nexus based on targeting patterns (including Uyghur cultural websites), operating hours, tool selection (PlugX with Chinese-language menus), and infrastructure linked to PRC-based ISPs. Kaspersky (2018) attributed the LuckyMouse data center campaign based on tools, domains, and TTPs consistent with Chinese-speaking actors.
entity_name: Shanghai Heiying Information Technology Co. Ltd. (上海黑英信息技术有限公司)
description:
APT27 is a Chinese state-associated cyber espionage group active since at least 2010. The DOJ's March 2025 indictments allege conduct "from 2011 to the present-day" and describes the group "as freelancers" who "conducted computer intrusions at the direction of the PRC's MPS and MSS and on their own initiative." The group is tracked under an unusually large number of aliases — at least 16 by Malpedia's count.
APT27 targets a broad range of sectors including government, defense, aerospace, technology, energy, manufacturing, telecommunications, and gambling, with victims across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. The group has also targeted Uyghur community websites and dissidents. 
Profero/Security Joes (2020) researchers observed "extremely strong links" between APT27 and a financially motivated threat actor deploying ransomware against gambling companies around 2020. This shift in focus was also noticed by TrendMicro/TalentJump (2020-2021) and PT Security (2020).
APT27 is associated with large number of campaigns, recently for the December 2024 breach of the US Treasury Department.  In July 2024, German domestic intelligence services BfV warned that APT27 was attacking European entities using new RSHELL variants.

campaigns.name: TG-3390 Cyberespionage Campaign
campaigns.description: Campaign documented across SecureWorks' three reports (2015, 2017, 2019). APT27/TG-3390/BRONZE UNION conducted sustained espionage operations targeting organizations across multiple sectors worldwide. SecureWorks assessed the group aimed to collect defense technology and capability intelligence, industrial intelligence, and political intelligence from governments and NGOs. Despite the 2015 public disclosure, BRONZE UNION continued operations, adapting tools and techniques.

campaigns.name: Operation Iron Tiger
campaigns.description: Trend Micro documented APT27/Iron Tiger shifting targets from East Asia to the United States, primarily targeting US defense contractors. The September 2015 report detailed the group's toolkit and operational patterns for stealing defense technology data. The campaign was notable for coinciding with APT27's broader expansion of targeting scope during this period.

campaigns.name: Central Asian National Data Center Compromise (Mongolia)
campaigns.description: Kaspersky discovered in March 2018 that APT27/LuckyMouse had compromised a national data center in Central Asia (subsequently identified by CyberScoop as Mongolia) beginning around October 2017. Through the data center, the group gained access to a wide range of government resources and injected malicious JavaScript into official government websites to conduct watering hole attacks, redirecting visitors to attacker domains.

campaigns.name: Gambling Sector Targeting
campaigns.description: Beginning in 2019, Trend Micro (working with Talent-Jump) investigated APT27's targeting of gambling companies, initially uncovering what they called Operation DRBControl.  In 2020, Profero/Security Joes similarly documented the group's pivot. Positive Technologies separately attributed a Polar ransomware attack (April 2020) to APT27. Profero noted the financial pivot was "unusual" for a cyberespionage group, speculating COVID-19 lockdowns may have motivated the shift. By 2023, Trend Micro confirmed continued targeting of Philippines-based gambling companies with updated SysUpdate (including Linux variants with DNS tunneling).

campaigns.name: HyperBro RAT Campaign
campaigns.description: According to Hive Pro, APT27 targeted against at least nine organizations across critical sectors worldwide from March to mid-September 2021. In January 2022, Germany's BfV warned that APT27 had been attacking German companies using these same vectors. The BfV assessed the intrusions focused on stealing business secrets and intellectual property, with potential supply chain attack attempts against victims' customers.

campaigns.name: US Treasury Department Breach (Silk Typhoon / BeyondTrust)
campaigns.description: In what became APT27's most high-profile operation, actors linked to Silk Typhoon/APT27 (subsequently identified as Yin Kecheng) compromised BeyondTrust's Remote Support SaaS platform beginning around September 2024. The breach, discovered by BeyondTrust on December 2, 2024, affected over 3,000 unclassified files across approximately 100 Treasury computers. Compromised offices included the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) — which administers US sanctions — and the Office of Financial Research. Files related to senior officials including Secretary Janet Yellen and Deputy Secretary Wally Adeyemo were reportedly compromised. The targeting of OFAC is particularly significant given China's strategic interest in understanding and potentially circumventing US sanctions enforcement. Microsoft published a concurrent report linking Silk Typhoon to IT supply chain targeting and an Ivanti VPN zero-day (CVE-2025-0282). Yin Kecheng was sanctioned in January 2025; both Yin and Zhou Shuai were indicted in March 2025.
